pages.title: Kaiapoi
pages.extract: Kaiapoi is a town just north of Christchurch on the east coast of the South Island of New Zealand. It lies 17 km from central Christchurch, and north of the Waimakariri River. The town is a separate community, but also a commuter suburb of its city neighbour.

pages.title: Kavala
pages.description: city in northern Greece, the principal seaport of eastern Macedonia and the capital of Kavala regional unit
pages.extract: Kavala (Greek: Καβάλα) is a city in Macedonia (Greece). Kavala is one of the most beautiful smaller cities in Greece offering a wide range of places of interest for tourism. A wealth of possibilities for excursions in the surrounding area, many beautiful not overcrowded beaches, archaeological sites and many places of natural beauty makes it a fun-filled vacation destination.

pages.title: Sapporo
pages.extract: Sapporo (札幌) is the capital and largest city of the northern island of Hokkaido. One of Japan's newest and most orderly cities, it has little in the way of traditional architecture. But what it lacks in "Japanese-ness" it makes up for with its lovely open, tree-filled boulevards to enjoy in summer and excellent snow (and facilities to cope with said snow) in the long winter. Its name means “the great dry field” in the Ainu language.

pages.title: Ķemeri National Park
pages.extract: Ķemeri National Park (Latvian: Ķemeru nacionālais parks) is a national park west of the city of Jūrmala, Latvia. The territory of the park is mostly occupied by forests and mires, the most significant of them being the Great Ķemeri Bog (Latvian: Lielais Ķemeru tīrelis). There are also several lakes, that are former lagoons of the Littorina Sea. Lake Kaņieris is a Ramsar site.

pages.title: Wars of the Roses
pages.description: dynastic civil war in England from 1455 to 1487
pages.extract:
The Wars of the Roses were a series of civil wars in 15th-century England, as rival barons fought for the crown. That crown also ruled Wales, Ireland, and dwindling parts of France, while Scotland was independent. In late medieval England, the Norman "feudal" system of strict male primogeniture began to be replaced by a cash economy. The more land you held, the richer you were, the more troops you could recruit, and so you won more land. The grandest barons might overshadow the king himself, and scheme to supplant him. 
Knights in armour, spearmen and bowmen, poxy peasants, great castles with towers and drawbridges and dungeons: these were the cinematic scenery of these Wars. Behind the scenes, social and technological changes were occurring that would eventually sweep them all away into history. The final battle ended not just the Wars, but the 1000-year period in Britain and Ireland that we call the Middle Ages, heralding the English Renaissance.

pages.title: Bardonecchia
pages.extract: Bardonecchia, or just Bardo among friends, is a town and comune in Piedmont in the upper Susa Valley. It is an important centre for winter sports with two ski areas: Colomion-Les Arnauds-Melezet and Jafferau. Bardonecchia is located in the center of a sunny valley, a starting point for enjoying the ski slopes in winter and the bike park in summer.
